title: Test de positionnement — Anglais (A1 à C2)
description:
Ce test situe votre niveau d'anglais sur l'échelle européenne CECRL, de A1 à C2.

25 questions à choix multiples et une courte rédaction — comptez environ 10 minutes. Aucune préparation n'est nécessaire.

Il n'y a ni réussite ni échec : le but est de vous orienter vers le parcours qui correspond vraiment à votre niveau. Répondez sans dictionnaire ni traducteur, et si vous ne savez pas, choisissez la réponse qui vous semble la plus probable et continuez. Les questions sont de difficulté croissante : il est normal de bloquer sur les dernières.

sections.name: Partie 1 — Grammaire et usage
sections.note: 16 questions, 1 point chacune. Difficulté croissante de A1 à C2.

questions.text: I ______ from Spain.
She ______ two brothers.
Yesterday I ______ to the cinema with my sister.
This film is ______ than the one we saw last week.
How ______ sugar would you like in your coffee?
I ______ in Lyon since 2015.
The report ______ by the finance team last week.
The colleague ______ helped me last month has left the company.
By the time we arrived, the meeting ______.
If I ______ more time, I would have finished the report.
I'm not used to ______ in public.
Not only ______ the deadline, but he also exceeded expectations.
______ for your support, the project would have failed.
The proposal was turned down, ______ came as no surprise to anyone.
The board insisted that the policy ______ reviewed immediately.
Little ______ that the deal would collapse within weeks.

sections.name: Partie 2 — Vocabulaire en contexte
sections.note: 7 questions, 1 point chacune. Vocabulaire courant puis professionnel.

questions.text: "What's your ______?" — "I'm a teacher."
I need to ______ an appointment with the doctor.
Please find the document ______ to this email.
The meeting has been ______ until next Tuesday.
Sales have increased ______ 15% this quarter.
Let's ______ up on this issue at our next meeting.
After six hours, the negotiations reached a complete ______.

sections.name: Partie 3 — Compréhension écrite
sections.note: 2 questions, 1 point chacune, sur un court email professionnel.

questions.helpText:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for sending the figures so quickly. Unfortunately, I won't be able to join Thursday's call — I'll be travelling back from the Manchester site all afternoon. Could we push it to Friday morning instead?

One thing before you meet: the Q3 forecast still doesn't include the new supplier costs, so the margin looks better than it really is.

Best,
Claire
questions.text: Why can't Claire join Thursday's call?

choices.t: She will be travelling back from another site.
She is on holiday that week.
She has already left the company.
She has not received the figures.

questions.helpText:
Hi Tom,

Thanks for sending the figures so quickly. Unfortunately, I won't be able to join Thursday's call — I'll be travelling back from the Manchester site all afternoon. Could we push it to Friday morning instead?

questions.text: What does Claire warn Tom about?

choices.t: Some costs are missing, so the margin looks too good.
The figures were sent to the wrong people.
The supplier has cancelled the contract.
The meeting room is not available.

sections.name: Partie 4 — Expression écrite
sections.note: Une seule question, courte, hors score automatique. C'est elle qui départage B1/B2 et C1/C2.

questions.text: In English, in 3 or 4 sentences: what are the advantages and disadvantages of working from home?
questions.helpText: Environ 40 mots. Écrivez sans dictionnaire ni traducteur — même avec des erreurs, cela nous aide à situer votre niveau.
